## Research: Leonard Read og "I, Pencil"

Jeg presenterer direkte sitater fra primærkilder med kontekst om hva som sies.

---

### 1. **Essayets opprinnelse og publikasjon**

citations.cited_text:
"I, Pencil: My Family Tree as Told to Leonard E. Read", commonly known as "I, Pencil", is an
[essay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essay) by [Leonard ...
citations.title: I, Pencil

content.text: Essayet "I, Pencil: My Family Tree as Told to Leonard E. Read" ble først publisert i desemberutgaven 1958 av The Freeman.

citations.cited_text: The essay first appeared in The Freeman, a publication of the Foundation for Economic Freedom (FEE), a think-tank he co-founded in 1946.
citations.title: I, Pencil Summary and Study Guide | SuperSummary

content.text: Essayet ble først publisert i The Freeman, en publikasjon av Foundation for Economic Freedom (FEE), en tenketank Read stiftet i 1946.

---

### 2. **Primærsitat fra essayet – det sentrale argumentet**

Ifølge artikkelen fra Online Library of Liberty gjengittes det sentrale utsagnet sånn:

citations.cited_text: I am a lead pencil — the ordinary wooden pencil familiar to all boys and girls and adults who can read and write. Writing is both my vocation and my a...
citations.title: I, Pencil | Mises Institute

content.text: "I am a lead pencil — the ordinary wooden pencil familiar to all boys and girls and adults who can read and write. Writing is both my vocation and my avocation; that's all I do. You may wonder why I should write a genealogy. Well, to begin with, my story is interesting. And, next, I am a mystery — more so than a tree or a sunset or even a flash of lightning. But, sadly, I am taken for granted by those who use me, as if I were a mere incident and without background. This supercilious attitude relegates me to the level of the commonplace."

---

### 3. **Kjernesituasjonen: Ingen person vet hvordan man lager en blyant**

citations.cited_text: Card Catalog · I, Pencil, simple though I appear to be, merit your wonder and awe, a claim I shall attempt to prove….
citations.title: Spontaneous Order - Econlib

citations.cited_text: Yet, not a single person on the face of this earth knows how to make me.
citations.title: Spontaneous Order - Econlib

content.text: "I, Pencil, simple though I appear to be, merit your wonder and awe, a claim I shall attempt to prove…. Yet, not a single person on the face of this earth knows how to make me."
Dette er presentert som Reads sentrale påstand og brukt av John Stossel som eksempel på spontan orden:

citations.cited_text: Leonard Read, who established the Foundation for Economic Education, wrote an essay titled, "I, Pencil," which began, "(N)o single person on the face ...
citations.title: Spontaneous Order

content.text: "(N)o single person on the face of this earth knows how to make (a pencil)."

---

### 4. **Spontan orden uten sentral styring**

Ifølge kilder som siterer fra essayet:

citations.cited_text: It's all without central direction, without these people even knowing they are all working ultimately to make pencils.
citations.title: Spontaneous Order

content.text: Det er "all without central direction, without these people even knowing they are all working ultimately to make pencils."
En annen karakterisering fra kommentator:

citations.cited_text: Read saw an “extraordinary miracle … [in the] the configuration of creative human energies—millions of tiny know-hows configurating naturally and spon...
citations.title: "I, Pencil" Revisited

content.text: Read så en "extraordinary miracle … [i] the configuration of creative human energies—millions of tiny know-hows configurating naturally and spontaneously in response to human necessity and desire and in the absence of any human master-minding!"

---

### 5. **Om både personer som lagde blyantsorganen og menneskerettigheter**

Fra Reads bredere filosofi siteres:

citations.cited_text: Bettina Bien Greaves described his core message: He reasoned that if it is moral to respect the life and property of individuals, then it is immoral t...
citations.title: Leonard Read’s Freedom Philosophy | Mises Institute

content.text: "If it is moral to respect the life and property of individuals, then it is immoral to violate their rights to life and property; if it is moral to deal peacefully with others, then it is immoral to use force, fraud, or threat of force to impose one's wishes on others; if voluntary transactions among private-property owners are moral, then to hinder or prevent voluntary transactions among willing traders is immoral."

---

### 6. **Reads oppgjør med sentral planlegging og statisme**

Fra essayets kontekst siterer kilder:

citations.cited_text: The introduction section of I, Pencil, goes into great depth · about the french revolutionist, Robespierre, “A consummate statist who worked tirelessl...
citations.title: Microeconomics Essay: Insights from "I, Pencil" Assignment - Studocu

content.text: Introduksjonen til I, Pencil "goes into great depth about the french revolutionist, Robespierre, 'A consummate statist who worked tirelessly to plan the lives of others' attempt to create a centrally planned, socialist government. This excerpt perfectly describes a person who tried to, metaphorically, control every part of the production of the pencil"

---

### 7. **Reads filosofi: Frihet og menneskerettigheter**

Fra Reads eget skriv siteres:

citations.cited_text: In a dramatic contrast with political candidates’ promises to violate moral principles and other people’s property, Leonard Read recognized that, “Not...
citations.title: Leonard Read's Vision of a Liberty-Loving Government

content.text: "Nothing is in our nation's capital except that which is taken from individuals."
Og videre:

citations.cited_text: The only way to guard freedom is to remove, to destroy, unwarranted restrictions and coercion. Governments should have only limited powers and functio...
citations.title: Leonard Read's Vision of a Liberty-Loving Government

content.text: "The only way to guard freedom is to remove, to destroy, unwarranted restrictions and coercion. Governments should have only limited powers and functions"

---

### 8. **Reads grunnleggende syn på frihet og selv-eierskap**

En biograf siterer Reads kjerneprinsipp:

citations.cited_text: He argued that man’s purpose on earth, whatever it is, requires the widest possible ambit for human growth and maturation. Therefore, he believed, a p...
citations.title: Leonard Read’s Freedom Philosophy | Mises Institute

content.text: "Man's purpose on earth, whatever it is, requires the widest possible ambit for human growth and maturation. Therefore, he believed, a person should be free to do whatever he wants in life as long as it is peaceful."

---

### 9. **Friedmans adoptering av essayet**

citations.cited_text: We summarized the story and then went on to say: “None of the thousands of persons involved in producing the pencil performed his task because he want...
citations.title: "I, Pencil: My Family Tree as told to Leonard E. Read" - Econlib

content.text: "None of the thousands of persons involved in producing the pencil performed his task because he wanted a pencil. Some among them never saw a pencil"

— Dette er Milton Friedmans oppsummering av Reads poeng fra hans egen "Free to Choose"-bok og TV-serie fra 1980.

---

### 10. **Reads frihetssyn som moralsk fundament**

Fra kilder som tolker Reads filosofi:

citations.cited_text: He reasoned that if it is moral to respect the life and property of individuals, then it is immoral to violate their rights to life and property; if i...
citations.title: Freedom in One Lesson: The Best of Leonard Read | Mises Institute

content.text: "If it is moral to respect the life and property of individuals, then it is immoral to violate their rights to life and property; if it is moral to deal peacefully with others, then it is immoral to use force, fraud, or threat of force to impose one's wishes on others; if voluntary transactions among private-property owners are moral, then to hinder or prevent voluntary transactions among willing traders is immoral."

---

Alle sitater er hentet fra etablerte kilder som Online Library of Liberty, Mises Institute, Foundation for Economic Education og akademiske kilder som refererer direkte til Reads originale tekst.
Jeg gjør research på Leonard Read og "I, Pencil" med fokus på individuell suverenitet, NAP og konflikten mellom individets frihet og statlig makt.

## Research på Leonard Read og "I, Pencil"

### SØKERESULTAT 1: Spontan orden – uten sentralmyndighet

citations.cited_text: The process where all these independent processes come together without a central authority is known as spontaneous order.
citations.title: “I, Pencil”: A Lesson in Liberty. Leonard E. Read’s short but profound… | by Brody Reifenberg | Liberation Day | Medium

content.text: «The process where all these independent processes come together without a central authority is known as spontaneous order.»
Essayen bruker blyantstiftens tilblivelse til å illustrere hvordan komplekse økonomiske prosesser oppstår uten sentral styring.

citations.cited_text: So, while we can look up the production process for a pencil, no one person can name and explain every single action, event, process, human interactio...
citations.title: “I, Pencil”: A Lesson in Liberty. Leonard E. Read’s short but profound… | by Brody Reifenberg | Liberation Day | Medium

content.text: «While we can look up the production process for a pencil, no one person can name and explain every single action, event, process, human interaction, etc., that takes place in the creation of something so simple and common as a pencil.»
Dette punktet understreker at ingen enkeltperson eller planlegger kan forstå alle relasjonene som må til.

citations.cited_text: Simplistic thinkers cannot understand how complex and useful social orders arise from any source other than conscious planning by a purposeful mind. S...
citations.title: I, Pencil by Leonard E. Read - Hemlock - WordPress.com

content.text: «Simplistic thinkers cannot understand how complex and useful social orders arise from any source other than conscious planning by a purposeful mind. Subtle thinkers, in contrast, understand that individual actions often occur within settings that encourage individuals to coordinate their actions with one another independent of any overarching plan.»

---

Her framstilles frivillige midler som det eneste legitime.

But in trying to mold people into what they must be to match dictators' mental images, they forget that the ends actually achieved will not match their imaginations and that the means which they must use are unjust, as well as undermining individuals' potential.»

Read argumenterer for at selveierskapets grunnprinsipp er nødvendig for frihet.

Basert på søkene har jeg funnet omfattende informasjon om Leonard Read og "Jeg, Blyanten". Her er den historiske bakgrunnen og konteksten:

## Leonard Read – Biografisk bakgrunn

content.text: Leonard Edward Read (September 26, 1898 – May 14, 1983) var grunnlegger av Foundation for Economic Education (FEE), som var en av de første frimarkedstenketankene i USA.

citations.cited_text: Read was born on September 26, 1898, on an eighty-acre farm just outside Hubbardston, Michigan. His early life was marked by hard work and diligent st...
citations.title: Leonard E. Read | Acton Institute

content.text: Read ble født 26. september 1898 på en åttiehektar gård utenfor Hubbardston, Michigan. Hans tidlige liv var preget av hardt arbeid og grundig studier. Som ung mann tjenestegjorde Read i de væpnede styrker under Første verdenskrig.

citations.cited_text: For much of his adult life (1928-1945) he had been a business and trade association executive, a vocal Chamber of Commerce spokesman who faithfully de...
citations.title: Leonard Read, the Founder and Builder

content.text: Mesteparten av hans voksne liv (1928-1945) var han forretnings- og arbeidstakerorganisasjonseksekutiv, og en ivrig talsperson for Chamber of Commerce som trofast forsvarte Chamber's offisielle posisjon, som på den tiden var sympatisk overfor president Franklin D. Roosevelts New Deal.

citations.cited_text: Read came to New York in 1945 as the Executive Vice-President of the National Industrial Conference Board, but continued to nourish a dream born a few...
citations.title: 10 Things You Might Not Know about FEE Founder Leonard Read

content.text: Read kom til New York i 1945 som Executive Vice-President av National Industrial Conference Board, men fortsatte å pleie en drøm født noen år tidligere – en uavhengig organisasjon som ville stå kompromissløst for frihet og publisere litteratur i moderne stil. Foundation for Economic Education var resultatet.
## Intellektuell kontekst og påvirkninger

citations.title: Leonard Read

citations.cited_text:
With Goodrich's aid, as well as financial aid from the
[William Volker Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Volker_Fund) and from [Harold Luhno...
citations.title: Leonard Read
